key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than manage light: they also improve film formation, crystal quality, carrier extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texture design is a multi-functional optimization lever that can raise efficiency and stability in perovskite photovoltaics, and may also benefit related optoelectronic devices.
method: Use nano/micro-textured surfaces to reduce reflection and boost light trapping.
Promote better perovskite-solution wetting to improve film coverage and uniformity.
Tune texture geometry to support larger grains, better crystal orientation, and lower residual stress.
evidence_signal: The paper is a review of very recently reported texture-related effects, summarizing observed gains in wetting, crystallinity, open-circuit voltage, and mechanical stability.
watch_item: Texture benefits may depend strongly on the specific geometry, processing route, and device stack, so gains are not automatically transferable across architectures.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
